sources.name: EPA ATTAINS
sources.summary: EPA disclaimers page: "Unless otherwise specified, geospatial data produced by the EPA is by default in the public domain." Individual documents may carry other conditions (not used). Applied to the ATTAINS assessment layer and StreamCat watershed metrics. Reviewer note: other EPA wording is mixed; re-read in a browser.
sources.credit: Water quality assessments and watershed data: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency

sources.name: OpenStreetMap via Overpass
sources.summary: OpenStreetMap boat ramps, put-ins and marinas near the gauge via the Overpass API; open data under ODbL, used with attribution.
sources.credit: Access points: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)

sources.name: Recreation.gov RIDB (federal recreation facilities)
sources.summary: data.gov catalog lists the Recreation Information Database under 'Creative Commons Attribution'; 'available to the public for various other uses'; federal agencies 'are responsible for the quality of data' and 'some data may be missing or incomplete'. Key: RIDB_API_KEY, header 'apikey', 50 requests a minute. Evidence: search-result 2026-10-21; the RIDB developer portal terms page could not be fetched (JavaScript app).
sources.credit: Recreation sites: Recreation.gov (RIDB)

sources.name: USGS HIVIS gaging-station cameras (NIMS API)
sources.summary: USGS copyrights and credits page: 'USGS-authored or produced data and information are considered to be in the U.S. Public Domain'; 'proper credit' is requested. The NIMS API describes its content as 'imagery from USGS gaging stations for public consumption'. Items the API lists as hidden (hideCam) are never shown. Evidence: search-result 2026-10-21 plus the API description read 2026-10-21. Key: USGS_API_KEY (api.waterdata.usgs.gov/signup).
sources.credit: Camera images: U.S. Geological Survey, HIVIS

sources.name: USGS The National Map (USGS Topo map service)
sources.summary: USGS FAQ: The National Map services and data are free with no license restrictions, public domain; USGS requests the credit line 'Map services and data available from U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program'. The FAQ does not name the basemap.nationalmap.gov host; applied to it by inference.
sources.credit: Map services and data available from U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program

sources.name: USDA NRCS SNOTEL (AWDB web service)
sources.summary: USDA policies page: most information on USDA websites is public domain and may be freely distributed or copied, with a byline credit requested ('U.S. Department of Agriculture'); some materials are copyrighted and labelled. No NRCS-specific SNOTEL terms page was found; applied from the USDA-wide policy.
sources.credit: Snow data: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Natural Resources Conservation Service

sources.name: NOAA Climate Prediction Center 8 to 14 day outlook (NWS map service)
sources.summary: NOAA/NWS disclaimer wording: information on government servers is public domain unless annotated; may not be altered and presented as official, may not imply NOAA endorsement. No CPC-specific page was found; applied from the NWS/NOAA disclaimer (some CPC international pages carry their own notice, not this product).
sources.credit: Outlook: NOAA Climate Prediction Center

sources.name: U.S. Drought Monitor
sources.summary: Permission page (map): 'The U.S. Drought Monitor is jointly produced by the National Drought Mitigation Center at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, the United States Department of Agriculture, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. Map courtesy of NDMC.' No separate data terms; data page footer is '©2026 - National Drought Mitigation Center'. Same credit applied to web-service values.
sources.credit: The U.S. Drought Monitor is jointly produced by the National Drought Mitigation Center at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, the United States Department of Agriculture, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. Map courtesy of NDMC.

sources.name: State fish and wildlife hatchery stocking records
sources.summary: Public state ArcGIS stocking layers (no auth), credited to the issuing agency. Shown as released species, date and count near the gauge; a release event, not a measure of fish now present.

sources.name: USGS WaterWatch
sources.summary: Retired by USGS in February 2026 per Drought.gov. Not used; the site computes its own percentile from USGS daily statistics.

sources.name: FEMA OpenFEMA API (Disaster Declarations Summaries)
sources.summary: OpenFEMA terms: "This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA." is the requested notice; cite the endpoint and version; do not modify content while claiming FEMA as the source; no FEMA or DHS logos. Quote extracted by a summarising tool; re-read in a browser.
sources.credit: Declarations: FEMA OpenFEMA (not endorsed by FEMA)

sources.name: NOAA CO-OPS tide predictions (api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov)
sources.summary: CO-OPS disclaimers: 'The information on government servers are in the public domain'; content 'shall not be modified in content and then presented as official government material'; 'NOS requests that attribution be given whenever NOS material is reproduced and re-disseminated.' Nearest station: list stations.json?type=tidepredictions and pick nearest by distance.
sources.credit: Tide predictions: NOAA National Ocean Service, CO-OPS

sources.name: EPA AirNow current air quality (airnowapi.org)
sources.summary: AirNow API FAQ: access 'is available to the public'; 'These data are not fully verified or validated and should be considered preliminary and subject to change'; each key has a call limit per service. Service: /aq/observation/current/ziplatlong/ (the 2026-10-01 replacement; the latLong service answers 410). Key: AIRNOW_API_KEY. Evidence: search-result 2026-10-21 and a live call read 2026-10-21.
sources.credit: Air quality: EPA AirNow and the reporting agency named on the row (preliminary data)

sources.name: National Center for Cold Water Safety, water temperature safety guide
sources.summary: Short attributed quotation of the guide's temperature categories with a link to the guide; the guide is the center's public safety material.
sources.credit: Guidance: National Center for Cold Water Safety
sources.evidence_phrase: labels 50-60F as 'Very Dangerous / Immediately Life-threatening'; categorizes 60-70F as Dangerous; advises caution below 70F and recommends thermal protection like wetsuits or drysuits
